articles.title: Is Zionism a form of racism?
articles.summary: New resolution by the UK’s Green Party says the answer is YES
articles.body:
Zionism should be treated as any other form of racism. That’s what members of the Green Party have agreed at their annual conference in the UK.

The resolution also expresses support for a, quote – ‘single democratic state throughout historic Palestine’. Israel has condemned the decision, calling it antisemitic.

So, what’s the motivation? And what impact will the Greens’ new policy have on British politics and beyond?

Guests: Tim Bale, Professor of politics at Queen Mary University of London.

Yossi Beilin, former Israeli Justice Minister.

Jonathan Lis, journalist and broadcaster

articles.title: LIV Golf: Competition secures potential $300m investment to emerge from restructuring
articles.summary: LIV Golf secures a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to emerge from restructuring before the 2027 season.
articles.body:
LIV Golf has secured a possible $300m in financing from BC Partners Credit in order to try to move forward with the 2027 season.

The league filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding , starting a court-supervised "restructuring process" that they hope to complete in early 2027.

It is unclear how much of the $300m LIV requires to start next year's schedule and which players will start the season.

The competition's participants are owed at least $45m (£33m) and have the option to leave.

However the agreement secures an extension for the league to discuss terms with its players, with talks now open until 25 October.

BBC Sport understands there is no obligation on players to sign on to LIV 2.0, regardless of whether they had previously signed multi-year contracts with LIV Golf.

League insiders see the committed investment as a "significant" step forward in the court-supervised restructuring process.

"Our goal is to facilitate LIV Golf's emergence from the restructuring process on sound financial footing and with renewed momentum heading into the 2027 season," said Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, in a statement.

Strained smiles and uncertainty - the strange end of LIV Golf 1.0

The credit firm, which provides financing to middle-market companies, said the funding would support the next phase of LIV Golf, under which players would become equity owners of both the league and its teams.

The financing remains subject to bankruptcy court approval and customary conditions.

"This investment is an important step forward for LIV Golf," said LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil in a statement.

"We're delivering on our major milestones, and while there is still work ahead, today marks meaningful progress toward a player-owned, team-focused, truly global league that complements the wider game and creates new opportunities for players, fans, partners, and the next generation of golfers."

Since LIV's controversial launch in 2021, more than $5bn (£3.7bn) has been spent by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), with major winners including Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau lured by lucrative contracts and vast prize money.

However, the future of the concept - and its star players - has been shrouded in uncertainty, with the 2026 season having ended early.

Documents in the petition outline money owed to LIV Golf's creditors with the 30 largest unsecured claims.

Two-time major winner Rahm tops that list with an unsecured claim of $7.5m (£5.5m).

DeChambeau ($5.7m - £4.2m), Dustin Johnson ($5.5m - £4.1m), Cameron Smith ($4.8m - £3.5m) and Tyrrell Hatton ($3.4m - £2.5m) are also among the top 30 creditors, as well as Brooks Koepka, who left to rejoin the PGA Tour in January but has an unsecured claim of $1.7m (£1.25m).

The total amount owed to the 14 current and former LIV players in the top 30 creditors is just over $45m (£33m).

A source familiar with the figures told BBC Sport the creditors list outlines the "amount owed and not paid for Q3" of 2026, not the full amounts.

Chapter 11 protection postpones a US company's obligations to its creditors, giving it time to reorganise its debts or sell parts of the business.

PIF is providing a bankruptcy loan of $49.6m (£36.6m) - called 'debtor in possession' (DIP) financing - to help fund the process.

images.caption: Image caption, LIV Golf was founded in 2021, with its first season taking place the following year

articles.title: Lifeline for LIV Golf with potential $300m investment as league looks to continue into 2027
articles.summary: BC Partners Credit hopes to put LIV Golf on "sound financial footing" and take "renewed momentum" into next year; LIV CEO says: "This marks meaningful progress toward a player-owned, team-focused, truly global league";  Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau among players owed millions of pounds
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands LIV has officially entered into an RSA - a Restricted Stock Award - with BC Partners and the league is confident it can move ahead with LIV 2.0.

The league lost its multi-billion-dollar funding from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) following the end of the 2026 campaign and filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States.

LIV hopes a court-supervised "restructuring process" can be completed early next year.

This new agreement includes a commitment from BC Partners to provide funding, subject to court approval, with a hearing scheduled on October 14 to approve the deal.

The arrangement secures an extension for the league to discuss terms with its players, with talks now open until October 25.

BC Partners Credit keen to put LIV on 'sound financial footing'

Sky Sports News understands there is no obligation on players, who are owed millions of pounds, to stick with LIV, regardless of whether they had previously signed multi-year contracts.

Ted Goldthorpe, partner and head of BC Partners Credit, said in a statement: "Our goal is to facilitate LIV Golf's emergence from the restructuring process on sound financial footing and with renewed momentum heading into the 2027 season."

BC Partners Credit will support the next stage of LIV, under which players would become equity owners of the league and its teams.

Major winners Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith and Dustin Johnson are among the players who signed with LIV following its creation in 2021 having been lured over from the PGA Tour.

Those golfers are some of the creditors listed with unsecured claims - Rahm heads that with 7.5m (£5.5m).

England's Tyrrell Hatton (£2.5m) is among the creditors, as is five-time major winner Brooks Koepka (£1.25m), who quit LIV to re-join the PGA Tour earlier this year.

LIV CEO: We believe ‌deeply in the future of this league'

LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil said: "This investment is an important ‌step forward for LIV Golf, and I want to thank Ted Goldthorpe and the entire BC Partners team for their conviction in what we're building.

"We believe ‌deeply in the future of this league and in the opportunity to build something distinctive alongside our players.

"We're delivering on our major milestones, and while there is still work ahead, today marks meaningful progress toward a player-owned, team-focused, truly global league that complements the wider game and creates new opportunities for players, fans, partners, and the next generation of golfers."

The league said the funding would enable it to move from the planning stage to operational execution.

articles.title: Pro-Palestine Greens challenge Labour’s grip on Starmer’s former seat
articles.summary: Green Party leader Zack Polanski hopes to shake Labour, which has held Holborn since the seat was created in 1983.
articles.body:
London, United Kingdom – At a meeting organised by a Muslim group in London ahead of a closely watched by-election, candidates from the Green and Liberal Democrat parties made their cases to residents beside empty seats. Their Labour and Conservative peers did not turn up.

Labour candidate Sagal Abdi Wali, a Somali-Muslim woman, told The Guardian she did not attend because she had a prior obligation and the invite had come too late. But the organiser, the Camden Muslim Network, pushed back, saying that she was invited earlier.

Fifteen candidates are in the race for former Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s old seat, including Green Party leader, Zack Polanski, who hopes to become a member of parliament.

Since the seat was created in Holborn and St Pancras in 1983, the Labour Party has held it. Starmer was first elected in 2015 and held it until his resignation, which triggered the by-election due to take place on Thursday.

At the meeting, the conversation ranged from local issues such as housing to Israel and Palestine.

Lib Dem candidate Patrick Stillman said his party had long called for Palestinian statehood but would not support a full boycott.

“I think the Labour government’s position is deeply cynical to apologise over Gaza, to recognise that mistakes have been made but to continue to sell arms to Israel, a country that’s committing a genocide,” he said to applause, adding that his party, which recently voted to describe Zionism as racism, supports a full boycott.

In leaflets sent to constituency residents, the Green Party focused on Abdi-Wali’s time as a Labour councillor and, more recently, as leader of Camden council – a role she secured in May.

One reads: “Bring change, Replace Labour, Vote Green”. On its reverse: “Every single Camden Labour councillor refused to sign the Palestine solidarity pledge or support pension fund divestment . Only Greens continue to stand firm on Palestine.”

Last month, Abdi-Wali spoke to the Camden New Journal, a local newspaper, about Gaza and the Green Party’s leaflets.

It was “obviously inaccurate” to say the Labour council did not feel strongly about the issue, she told the paper. “I want to focus on making sure that we’re able to put the message of what [Foreign Secretary] Ed Miliband is now doing with the government and on Palestine and Israel and Gaza and the West Bank.”

In January, Camden Friends of Palestine (CFOP), a local group that formed in response to Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, presented a petition to the local council with 4,000 signatures calling for the council to divest its pension fund from companies involved in Israel’s actions in the occupied Palestinian territories.

Abdi-Wali, then a Labour councillor, did not support the motion. Rather than committing to divestment, most councillors voted to refer the question to the pension board for review.

“My impression of her and her politics is that she’s just really incredibly silent on everything, if there isn’t a career motive for her, and that’s kind of disappointing,” said 38-year-old Shadin, a resident and CFOP organiser, who plans to vote for Polanski.

“Watching a livestreamed genocide has made a lot of people that I know … disengage from mainstream politics or parliamentary politics”.

Like many London constituencies, a key issue is housing.

According to a “2026 state of the borough” report by Camden council, 8,380 households were on the waiting list for social housing at the end of March 2025, “an increase of 9.5 percent on the year before.”

On Friday, in the constituency’s more affluent area of Primrose Hill, one resident said they would vote for Labour in the upcoming election, while another believed that regardless of who wins, life will not change.

In Camden, another resident told Al Jazeera that while they live in the area, they were not aware of the election, as Labour canvassers buzzed to gain entry into a nearby estate in the background.

As both parties make their final efforts to secure victory, recent polls predict a close race.

In the 2024 general election, Starmer won the seat with 49 percent. Andrew Feinstein , a pro-Palestine independent candidate came second, with 19 percent. The British gambling firm Ladbrokes and Stats for Lefties, which examines polling, both predict Labour will win.

images.caption: Labour Party candidate Sagal Abdi-Wali and Leader of Britain's Green Party, Zack Polanski [AFP]

articles.title: Martínez-Almeida: “Madrid es una de las cinco grandes ciudades del deporte mundial”
articles.standfirst: El alcalde destaca el calendario deportivo de la capital durante la presentación del Open de España presented by Madrid
articles.summary: El alcalde destaca el calendario deportivo de la capital durante la presentación del Open de España presented by Madrid
articles.body: El Open de España presented by Madrid 2026 ya está en marcha y este año, pese a la ausencia de Jon Rahm, el torneo puede presumir de un plantel de enorme calidad que invita a no perderse una cita ya consolidada en el calendario deportivo de la capital de España. En la sede del torneo, el Club de Campo Villa de Madrid, ha tenido lugar un acto de presentación con la presencia del alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez-Almeida; el presidente de la RFEG, Juan Guerrero-Burgos; el promotor del torneo, Gerard Tsobanian; y los jugadores Marco Penge, Patrick Reed y Ángel Ayora. Todos ellos, flanqueados por la copa de campeón del Masters de Augusta y la Jarra de Clarete del British Open, y es que por segundo año el ganador del abierto nacional volverá a recibir como premio la clasificación directa para estos dos torneos. El regidor de la capital, que apareció en el Club de Campo montado en un autobús de la EMT decorado con imágenes del torneo, destacó el posicionamiento internacional tanto del torneo como de la ciudad. “Es un gran acontecimiento en el calendario deportivo de Madrid, como la Fórmula 1, el Mutua de tenis o la final de la Champions. El Open ya tiene personalidad propia y cada año entre todos hemos construido un torneo mejor. Madrid es una de las cinco grandes ciudades del deporte mundial junto con Nueva York, París, Los Ángeles y Londres”, declaró. De hecho, según el ranking que realiza la agencia Burson, esto es así y la sexta de esta clasificación es Barcelona. El listado de participantes este año cuenta con nombres como el citado Penge, vigente campeón, Tyrrell Hatton, Sergio García, Justin Rose, Shane Lowry, Nicolai Hojgaard, Patrick Reed, Francesco Molinari, Bubba Watson, Justin Reed, Ludvig Aberg, Thomas Detry, Alex Noren, Adrian Meronk… y una legión de españoles que vienen pisando muy fuerte como Eugenio López-Chacarra, David Puig, Ángel Ayora, Josele Ballester o Nacho y Manu Elvira. Tsobanian, el encargado dar forma al torneo, declaró: “Me comprometí hace años a que el torneo creciera y estamos cumpliendo. El dilema este año es a quién seguir en el campo. Año tras año hemos subido el nivel y nunca habíamos llegado a lo que tenemos en esta edición”. Asimismo, Juan Guerrero-Burgos puso en valor el crecimiento experimentado: “Esto no sería posible sin tantos apoyos. Por nombre de jugadores estamos ante el mejor Open de España. Se está tratando de buscar la excelencia y en ese sentido este torneo es una referencia. Hay que invitar a los aficionados a que vengan y no se pierdan este espectáculo”.

articles.title: LIV Golf encuentra su mecenas: un nuevo inversor aportará 300 millones
articles.standfirst: La compañía financiera BC Partners Credit quiere asegurar la permanencia del circuito
articles.summary: La compañía financiera BC Partners Credit quiere asegurar la permanencia del circuito
articles.body: La compañía financiera BC Partners Credit anunció que aportará una inversión de 300 millones de dólares (unos 265 millones de euros) para el nuevo proyecto LIV 2.0 de golf, la liga a la que Arabia Saudí decidió dejar de inyectar dinero el pasado agosto al concluir la temporada. BC Partners Credit informó en un comunicado de que este fondo busca facilitar el proceso de reestructuración de LIV sobre una base financiera ″sólida, sostenible y centrada en el trabajo en equipo″ con el fin de asegurar su futuro a partir de 2027. El anuncio de la entidad de crédito privado llega un mes después de que LIV comunicara la solicitud de bancarrota ante un tribunal de Nueva York y esbozara algunos de los ejes de su nuevo proyecto, en el que pretende que los jugadores pasan a ser copropietarios tanto del circuito como de los equipos que lo integran y que tengan voz en el diseño de la competición. ″Otorgar a los jugadores una participación real y activa en la liga y los equipos es una oportunidad única en el golf profesional y alinea a todos en torno al éxito a largo plazo del producto, tanto para el deporte como para los aficionados", sostiene el director de BC Partners Credit, Ted Goldthorpe. "Esta inversión es un paso importante para LIV Golf. Creemos firmemente en el futuro de esta liga y en la oportunidad de construir algo singular junto a nuestros jugadores. Estamos cumpliendo con nuestros objetivos principales, y aunque aún queda trabajo por hacer, este acuerdo marca un progreso significativo hacia una liga verdaderamente global, propiedad de los jugadores y centrada en los equipos, que complementa el golf en general y crea nuevas oportunidades para jugadores, aficionados, socios y la próxima generación de golfistas", afirma Scott O'Neil, director ejecutivo de LIV Golf. Para la empresa financiera, el formato por equipos de LIV, una de sus señas de identidad desde que nació en 2022, al igual que la ausencia de corte en los torneos, ofrece ″una experiencia única y valiosa que puede complementar y fortalecer el ecosistema del golf en general″. "Invitamos a quienes quieran ayudar a construir una liga de golf sólida y sostenible a unirse a nosotros", añade Goldthorpe. Este acuerdo incluye el compromiso de BC Partners de proporcionar financiación, sujeto a la aprobación judicial, y está prevista una audiencia para el 14 de octubre para aprobar el acuerdo. Además, garantiza una prórroga para que el LIV pueda negociar las condiciones con sus jugadores, y las conversaciones estarán abiertas hasta el 25 de octubre. Entre las principales estrellas que aún sigue ligados a LIV por sus contratos están el español Jon Rahm y el estadounidense Bryson DeChambeau, si bien aún no han confirmado si tienen intención de seguir o no ligados al nuevo proyecto. En el caso de Rahm, principal acreedor de LIV con 7,4 millones de dólares (unos 6,5 millones de euros), según la documentación presentada tras la solicitud de quiebra, afirmó el pasado día 15 que no será hasta final de temporada cuando aclare si participará o no en LIV 2.0 al asegurar que debe resolverse "un largo proceso legal antes de que muchas cosas puedan concretarse".

images.caption: Jon Rahm, en un torneo de LIV Golf. LIV Golf

articles.title: Wyndham Clark Steps Back To Save His Career
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark credits therapy and stepping back from the grind for his survival as U.S. Open champ, proving mental health wins on Tour.
articles.body:
Life piles on fast for anyone chasing a dream. Deadlines, bills, and family events crowd the calendar alongside tee times. The constant buzz of bad news and urgent headlines never stops. Many golfers tell themselves to keep grinding until the wheels start to fall off. That is why the conversation is shifting toward taking a break for mental health.

It is not about going soft. It is about survival. You would not run a car for years without an oil change. Expecting to break 80 while using mud-caked clubs is something you would never do. The same logic applies to the human mind. Ignoring mental health does not make a player tougher. It just delays the crash.

According to MyGolfSpy , Wyndham Clark, the U.S. Open champ, opened up about the battles that nearly ended his career. The pressure was immense after losing his mom. He faced challenges that threatened to take him off Tour completely. Therapy and sports psychology are the reasons he is still competing at the highest level. He did not lose his edge by talking about what set him back. Instead, he found a way to use those struggles to his advantage.

MyGolfSpy reported that Clark is just one of several elite athletes who have embraced this path. Michael Phelps, the most decorated Olympian alive, publicly discussed his struggle with depression and the treatment he received. Kevin Love, a five-time NBA all-star, has integrated mental health permanently into his platform. These competitors show that facing mental challenges does not weaken a player. It strengthens their resolve.

The pressure for most golfers is not winning a major or Game 7. It is the everyday grind. Think about the last time nothing was clicking on the course. You worked longer, stayed up later, and skipped lunch. You told yourself to push through. That approach might fix things in the moment, but the real reset never comes during those frantic hours. MyGolfSpy notes that change comes from taking a step back. It requires space and time to breathe. Some golfers will play rounds, while others will hike, fish, or hang with their kids. Some will do nothing at all. That is the point. Every golfer deserves that time and attention.

The narrative around mental toughness in golf is finally changing. For decades, the sport demanded that players hide their struggles. Now, the data shows that addressing mental health preserves careers. Wyndham Clark's story proves that therapy is a tool for success, not a sign of weakness. When a player admits they are struggling, they gain a support system.

This system helps them handle the pressure of the PGA Tour. The game is hard enough without the added weight of silence. Golfers who take breaks return sharper. They are not broken; they are recharged. This approach allows players to enjoy the sport again. It keeps the passion alive when the results are not going their way. The best players know that mental fitness is just as important as physical fitness.

Golf fans should expect to see more open conversations from the tour. The days of suffering in silence are over. Players like Clark are leading the way by showing vulnerability. This transparency helps the next generation of golfers.

articles.title: Ryder Cup: Luke Donald warns against Team Europe complacency as Jim Furyk claims Team USA are underdogs at Adare Manor
articles.summary: Luke Donald is looking to claim a third consecutive Ryder Cup victory for Team Europe; American captain Jim Furyk says he will make changes to try and earn an away win in Ireland; watch the 2027 Ryder Cup exclusively live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Donald is aiming to become the first captain in history to lead a team to three consecutive Ryder Cup victories, having masterminded a 16.5-11.5 win over the Americans in the 2023 edition Rome and a historic 15-13 triumph at Bethpage Black last September.

Team Europe have won their last seven home Ryder Cups and are looking to extend that run in the centenary edition, live on Sky Sports , while Furyk has made changes to Team USA's qualification criteria and backroom analytics in a bid to end their winless away streak.

President Cup captain Brandt Snedeker said his victorious American team was "going to be a problem" in Ireland, despite needing a final-day singles comeback to avoid an embarrassing home defeat to the International Team, with Donald aware of the challenge his side will face.

"I have zero complacency about how strong the United States are going to be," Donald said in a press conference. "They always are. On paper, they tend to be stronger than us through the world rankings.

"Obviously we have a great record at home but again, zero complacency. I've seen what Jim [Furyk] has been doing behind the scenes, changing the stats, changing the qualification system. He is very, very motivated to come here and put up a good fight.

"I'm just as motivated to keep finding those edges for my team as well but you know and I know that the US will be very strong."

Furyk has been involved in every Ryder Cup in some capacity since 1997 and captained Team USA during their 2018 loss at Le Golf National, with the former US Open champion taking learnings from past contests into his second captaincy stint.

"We know what we're up against," Furyk insisted. "We also know that it's been 34 years since we won in Europe - there's no secret. I'm going to hear it over and over again, so I'm going to embrace it.

"Luke and Dodo [Edoardo Molinari] have the opportunity to set the golf course up, trying to tip the scales to Europe. We're the underdogs. I know it's always been played, we come in, the Americans seem to be the favourites.

"This year, there's no chance that that could happen. We're the underdogs. We understand that. We've got a lot of work ahead of us."

On who the favourites are, Donald responded: "For us, underdog is a mentality. We always want to prove something to ourselves, to the rest of the world.

"We understand that being at home is an advantage but we also know that the US are very strong."

Team USA have won just eight points from 34 in foursomes - where two players alternate shots with one ball - across their last four Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup matches, with just three from 16 against Europe.

Furyk is keen for all of his potential American players to be available for a fact-finding trip to Adare Manor next summer ahead of the Scottish Open and The Open, with the 56-year-old also looking at other ways to try and boost their hopes of a first away win since 1993.

"I'm going to ask this team to do more than any other United States team has in the past," Furyk insisted. "I changed a few things immediately upon taking the captaincy. You're always coming up with new, creative ways to create that team atmosphere and that bond, but we've got a lot to work on.

"I've had some ideas and thoughts about how I thought Team USA could and should be run in the future. I think Terry Clark, our (PGA of America) CEO, and I are aligned on those."

On the poor foursomes record, Furyk added: "It is not an anomaly. There's some issues - we understand that. Not something I'm very happy with. I plan on making some changes.

"As captains we need to do a better job - not only putting the folks into good pairings in good positions, but I don't think we are preparing for those matches in a proper way."

articles.title: Ryder Cup 2027: Captain Jim Furyk says USA will be 'underdogs' at Adare Manor
articles.summary: United States Ryder Cup captain Jim Furyk says his team will be "underdogs" when they attempt to end more than 30 years of pain on European soil in next year's edition at Adare Manor.
articles.body:
United States captain Jim Furyk says his team will be "underdogs" when they attempt to end more than 30 years of pain on European soil in next year's Ryder Cup at Adare Manor.

The Americans have not claimed an away Ryder Cup victory since 1993, losing all seven contests in Europe since that victory at The Belfry.

Furyk, who oversaw a 17½-10½ loss to Europe in France in 2018, was handed a second stint as captain earlier this year following Keegan Bradley's team's defeat to Luke Donald's Europe at Bethpage Black in 2025.

"We know what we are up against, we also know it's been 34 years since we won in Europe. There is no secret, I'm going to hear it over and over again so I am going to embrace it," Furyk said during a news conference at Adare Manor in County Limerick.

"Luke and Dodo [Edoardo Molinari, vice-captain] have the opportunity to set the golf course up, tip the scales for Europe. We're the underdogs.

"I know it's always been the Americans who seem to be the favourites, this year there is no chance that could happen. We are the underdogs, we understand that and we have a lot of work ahead of us."

Speaking to BBC Sport NI, Donald said he was not entirely certain about Furyk's assertion that Europe will be favourites in Ireland.

"I think reading between the lines, he is very focused on this Ryder Cup and wants to make amends for what happened in 2018 and the last two Ryder Cups," said Donald.

"He's going to bring a very strong team, that's why I'm not quite so certain that they'll definitely be the underdogs. They'll be strong and will be coming for us but we'll be ready."

Donald, who won four Ryder Cups as a player, led Europe to a resounding 16½-11½ win in Rome in 2023 before masterminding last year's dramatic 15-13 triumph at Bethpage - Europe's first away win since 2012.

The 48-year-old Englishman made just one change to his team for last year's win but he admits there may be more of a "shift" for the centenary edition, having invited potential rookies Eugenio Chacarra, Angel Ayora, Alex Fiztpatrick and Kristoffer Reitan to a scouting trip at Adare Manor last month.

"Certainly something unique was that we had a lot of continuity with the last two teams but I expect that to shift a little bit for this one," added Donald, who is hoping to become the first captain to win three Ryder Cups in a row after victories in Rome and New York.

"There's always new talent coming up, it's about recognising that, getting to know new players, understanding how they tick and coming up with a great plan for success."

Furyk plans to change foursomes approach

In 2018, Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas - two of the three youngest players on Furyk's team - starred as they won three out of four points as a foursomes and fourballs pairing.

With 21-year-old Jackson Koivun having impressed during an unbeaten Presidents Cup debut in last month's comeback victory over the Internationals in Chicago, Furyk says he is excited to inject more youth into the US side.

"I really love the guys who have played for us in the past few years," the 56-year-old, who played in nine consecutive Ryder Cups between 1997 and 2014, told the BBC.

"We have tough, gritty veterans who have been around the block, and I'm excited, we have a lot of great, young talent who have yet to play in this cup and I'd bet two or three of them will be at Adare."

During the news conference, Furyk said he will ask his team to "do more than any American team has in the past" to seal an elusive away win and vowed to address his side's dismal recent record in foursomes.

The US won just three points from a possible 16 in the alternate-shot format over the past two Ryder Cups.

"I know those numbers very well. I've lived them the last four," said Furyk.

"It's not an anomaly. There's some issues. We understand that. Not something I'm very happy with. I plan on making some changes.

"As captains we need to do a better job – not only putting the folks into good pairings in good positions, but I don't think we are preparing for those matches in a proper way."

The 2027 Ryder Cup - the second to be staged in Ireland after the K Club in 2006 - will take place on 17-19 September.

articles.title: Guernsey FC keep up winning run with Newhaven victory
articles.summary: Guernsey FC come from a goal down to win 3-1 at Newhaven in the Southern Combination Premier Division.
articles.body:
Guernsey FC came from a goal down to win 3-1 at Newhaven in the Southern Combination Premier Division.

Newhaven started well - Ezra Roag forced a smart save from Seb Shepherd in the second minute after the Green Lions had given the ball away before Lee Robinson headed the hosts ahead eight minutes later.

Guernsey's evening got worse when experienced defender Jamie Dodd came off with an 18th-minute rib injury before Jacob Fallaize was sin-binned for a remark to an official two minutes later.

But when they returned to their full complement of 11 men Guernsey improved as they turned the game around in an eight-minute spell.

First Sam Murray poked home George Goubert's cross from the left for his second goal in as many games after returning from injury.

Then teenager Goubert headed home an excellent 43rd-minute Dylan Graham cross from the right to put the islanders in front at the interval.

It was 3-1 moments after the break as as record goalscorer Ross Allen poked in Graham's cross from a quickly-taken corner.

Fin Du Port saw an effort curl just wide of the far post midway through the second half for Guernsey while Graham blazed an effort high and wide 12 minutes later.

The win was Guernsey's third in succession and keeps them seventh in the table.
